sources.title: Atılım Güneş Baydin, Barak A. Pearlmutter, Alexey Andreyevich Radul, and Jeffrey Mark Siskind, Automatic Differentiation in Machine Learning: a Survey
sources.locator: Journal of Machine Learning Research 18 (2018), pp. 1–43; complete relevant reasoning read in §§3 and 5: computation traces §3 pp. 7–8; forward accumulation §3.1 pp. 8–11; reverse accumulation, adjoint summation, and scalar-output gradient §3.2 pp. 11–12; operation-count and storage comparison pp. 12–13; implementation overhead §5 pp. 20–21.

contents.name: A finite execution trace composes elementary operations, with chain-rule derivatives evaluated on the trace
Reverse accumulation seeds the scalar output, traverses operations backward, and adds contributions from each downstream use at a shared node
The reverse sweep computes all input derivatives of a scalar output in one pass, with the operation-count and storage caveats stated in the survey

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.S096, Matrix Calculus for Machine Learning and Beyond, Lecture 5 Part 3: Forward and Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation
sources.locator: Complete 16-page lecture note read; §8.3 computational graphs and forward/reverse accumulation, PDF pp. 6–11; §8.4 input/output cost scaling and reverse-mode tape storage, PDF pp. 11–12.

contents.name: Computational-graph path products and the local reverse rule summing over all children of a node
Reverse mode is efficient for scalar objectives with many inputs and records intermediate values for the reverse pass
